cards.text: The word of the LORD comes to Joel son of Pethuel. Joel calls out to the elders and to everybody who lives in the land. And he opens with a question that would make anybody put their phone down: "Has anything like this ever happened in your days or in the days of your fathers?"

cards.question: Joel says what's happened is so big that one generation can't keep it to themselves. What does he tell them to do with it?

answers.text: Carve it into the city gate

cards.text: So what is this thing nobody's ever seen? Locusts, and not one kind of locust but FOUR: the devouring locust, the swarming locust, the young locust and the destroying locust.

cards.question: Joel says each kind of locust eats what the kind before it left behind.

cards.text: Four waves, each one eating what the last one left. It's a cookie box in the break room where one guy takes the chocolate chip ones, the next takes the sprinkles, the next takes the broken ones, and the fourth guy walks in and eats the CRUMBS.
Then Joel calls out: wake up, you drunkards, and weep, wail, all you drinkers of wine. That is NOT the alarm anybody wants to wake up to.

cards.question: Why does Joel tell the drinkers of wine to wail?

answers.text: The sweet wine is cut off from them
Their wine jars have been smashed
The king has banned all their feasts

cards.text: Then the picture changes: a nation has invaded, powerful and without number, with teeth like a lion's and fangs like a lioness's. Without number? I spent years counting the dust falling in a junk drawer, and friend, that dust never had FANGS.

cards.question: This invader lays waste the grapevine and goes after the fig tree. What does it do to the fig tree?

answers.text: Splinters it and strips the bark
Pulls it up by the roots

cards.text: The bark gets thrown away, and the branches have turned white. Then Joel says to wail like a virgin dressed in sackcloth, grieving for the husband of her youth.

cards.question: With the crops ruined, the ___ and drink offerings are cut off from the house of the LORD.
The priests who minister before the LORD are in mourning.

cards.text: The field is ruined, and the land itself mourns. The grain is destroyed, the new wine is dried up and the oil fails.

cards.question: Joel tells the farmers and the vinedressers to celebrate what's left of the harvest.

cards.text: The wheat, the barley, the whole harvest of the field has perished. Then the orchard: the grapevine, the fig, the pomegranate, the palm and the apple, every tree withered.

cards.question: With every tree in the orchard withered, Joel says surely the ___ of mankind has dried up.

cards.text: Now Joel turns to the priests, the ministers of the altar. Put on sackcloth, he tells them, and lament.

cards.question: Joel tells the priests to put on sackcloth. How long does he tell them to stay in it?

cards.text: Sackcloth, all night long, because the grain and drink offerings are withheld from the house of their God. And I thought sleeping under old takeout menus in a junk drawer was rough.
Then Joel calls for a fast that's set apart, and a solemn assembly. This is the meeting you do NOT skip.

cards.question: Joel says to gather the ___ and all the residents of the land to the house of the LORD.
Once everyone is gathered at the house of the LORD, what does Joel tell them to do?

cards.text: Then Joel cries out, "Alas for the day!" He's talking about the Day of the LORD.

cards.question: Joel says the Day of the LORD is still far off.
Joel says the Day of the LORD will come as ___ from the Almighty.

cards.text: Joel asks: hasn't the food been cut off right before their eyes, and joy and gladness from the house of God? The seeds lie shriveled under the clods, and the storehouses are in ruins.

cards.question: The granaries are broken down too. Why?

answers.text: A flood has washed them out

cards.text: And it's not just the people. The cattle groan, and the herds wander in confusion, like everybody in a parking garage trying to remember where they parked.

cards.question: The herds wander in confusion because they have no pasture.

cards.text: Even the flocks of sheep are suffering. Then Joel prays, "To You, O LORD, I call."

cards.question: Joel tells the LORD what has consumed the open pastures and scorched the trees of the field. What is it?
Joel isn't the only one calling out. Who else does he say pant for the LORD?

cards.text: Even the beasts of the field pant for the LORD, because the streams of water have dried up and fire has consumed the open pastures. Joel calls to the LORD, and even the animals pant for Him.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 14 quotes "To You, O LORD, I call.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The question's setup says one generation 'can't keep it to themselves.' That rules out the wrong answer 'Keep it among the priests' and points straight to the next generation, which nearly gives the answer away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card restates Joel 1:4, which cards 3 and 4 already covered ('Four waves, each one eating what the last one left'). It adds only a joke and doesn't move the passage forward. The joke should ride on a card that carries a new moment.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: Joel 1:6-7 says 'a nation has invaded My land' and 'laid waste My grapevine and splintered My fig tree,' so the LORD speaks of the land and the trees as His own. Card 8 says only 'a nation has invaded,' and card 9 says 'the grapevine' and 'the fig tree.' The baker misses that the LORD is the speaker and that the land is His.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Card 13 has just said the field is ruined, the grain destroyed and the new wine dried up. That makes 'celebrate what's left of the harvest' plainly false, so the true or false answer is given away. The card also never asks about what Joel actually tells the farmers (be dismayed, wail).

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'wealth' is defensible. With the whole harvest and every orchard tree gone, a baker could argue that the wealth of mankind has dried up.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Card 7 has just quoted 'Alas for the day!', and both wrong answers ('comfort' and 'blessing') are positive. The setup rules them out, so 'destruction' is the only answer that fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card carries three things: the food and joy cut off, the seeds shriveled under the clods, and the storehouses in ruins.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Joel 1:16 says 'before our very eyes' and 'the house of our God,' so the speaker counts himself in. The card changes this to 'right before their eyes,' which takes him out of the group the text puts him in.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Joel 1:6 says 'a nation has invaded My land,' and card 8 told the baker so. Because of that, a baker could argue the wrong answer 'Raiders have torn them down' is right.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The question says the trees were 'scorched.' Scorching points straight to fire, so the wording itself rules out hail and frost.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question says 'Joel isn't the only one calling out.' Joel 1:20 says the beasts 'pant for You.' It never says they call out.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card restates the answer card 16 just revealed ('Even the beasts of the field pant for the LORD'). Its last sentence ('Joel calls to the LORD, and even the animals pant for Him') recaps cards 14 and 16. Only the dried-up streams is new.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
